import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# --- Data Preprocessing ---
# Combine date and time into a single datetime object for time series analysis
df['datetime'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'] + ' ' + df['time'])

# Extract the hour and the day of the week
df['hour'] = df['datetime'].dt.hour
df['day_of_week'] = df['datetime'].dt.day_name()

# --- Data Aggregation ---
# Create a pivot table to aggregate total sales by day of the week and hour
heatmap_data = df.pivot_table(
    values='total',
    index='day_of_week',
    columns='hour',
    aggfunc='sum',
    fill_value=0
)

# Ensure the days are in chronological order
day_order = ['Monday', 'Tuesday', 'Wednesday', 'Thursday', 'Friday', 'Saturday', 'Sunday']
heatmap_data = heatmap_data.reindex(day_order)

# --- Visualization ---
# Set the style and figure size
plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid')
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(16, 9))

# Create the heatmap
sns.heatmap(
    heatmap_data,
    cmap='YlGnBu',
    linewidths=.5,
    annot=False,  # Annotations would be too cluttered
    cbar_kws={'label': 'Total Sales ($)'},
    ax=ax
)

# --- Customization and Labels ---
# Set title and labels with appropriate font sizes
ax.set_title('Peak Sales Times: Hourly Sales by Day of the Week', fontsize=18, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
ax.set_xlabel('Hour of Day (24-hour format)', fontsize=12, labelpad=10)
ax.set_ylabel('Day of the Week', fontsize=12, labelpad=10)

# Customize tick parameters for better readability
ax.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=0, labelsize=10)
ax.tick_params(axis='y', rotation=0, labelsize=10)

# Format the color bar to show currency
cbar = ax.collections[0].colorbar
cbar.ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.StrMethodFormatter('${x:,.0f}'))
cbar.ax.tick_params(labelsize=10)
cbar.ax.set_ylabel('Total Sales ($)', rotation=270, labelpad=15, fontsize=12)

# --- Save the Figure ---
# Save the final visualization to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
